title: split-presubmit-test-profiles-for-rust-and-go + add dep-freeze-adapter to stabilize CI
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: presubmit CI has been a major source of noisy failures and slow feedback for mixed-language changes. Our current single presubmit matrix runs broad rust+go test profiles and a monolithic dependency install step that invalidates caches frequently. This PR splits language-specific presubmit profiles, tightens cache keying, and adds a lightweight 'dep-freeze-adapter' that produces minimal, per-profile lock overlays to reduce transitive churn. Goal: faster, more stable presubmit runs with clearer failure attribution and fewer full-cache evictions. Changes in this PR: 1) Introduce two separate presubmit workflows: .github/workflows/presubmit-rust.yml and .github/workflows/presubmit-go.yml. Each workflow exposes narrow profiles (quick, integration, full) instead of a single combined job matrix. 2) Add tooling/presubmit/profiles.yaml which declares canonical testprofiles and their resource buckets; used by workflow generation and local dev shim. 3) Implement ci/scripts/dep-freeze-adapter.go: a small Go binary that inspects workspace manifests, computes a minimal freeze file for the requested profile (pins top-level deps, prunes optional transitive sets), and emits layered lockfiles that are cached by CI. 4) Change CI cache keying logic in ci/cache/keying.go to include profile:name and language hash (not the full lockfile hash) to avoid unnecessary invalidation when unrelated language changes land. 5) Add a lightweight presubmit bootstrap script scripts/ci-bootstrap.sh that coordinates fetch+freeze+setup in <60s for quick profiles. 6) Docs: docs/ci/presubmit.md updated with examples and local reproduction steps. Motivation and tradeoffs: the dep-freeze-adapter favors deterministic presubmit installs and faster cache warmups at the cost of maintaining a small compatibility shim. It does not replace canonical dependency locks for releases; it only produces ephemeral overlays for CI profiles. Migration plan: workflows added in this PR run in parallel with the existing combined presubmit for two weeks (opt-in via toggles). After monitoring (SLAs: 30% median runtime reduction target for quick profiles, 50% fewer cache-miss full installs), we'll flip the default and remove the monolithic workflow. Checklist: - [x] Add separate presubmit workflow files - [x] Implement dep-freeze-adapter prototype and unit tests - [x] Update cache keying and bootstrap script - [x] Update docs and local dev shim - [x] Run dogfood against redwood/* and redwood-sdk-python for two days - [x] Add metrics to presubmit dashboards (runtime, cache-hit) Related: ENG-2653 (reduce-rust-presubmit-flakiness), infra notes in Linear ENG-2874.

release_notes: Staged CI changes: split Rust/Go presubmit workflows, introduce dep-freeze-adapter for profile-specific minimal lock overlays, improved cache keying and a faster bootstrap script. This should reduce presubmit runtime for quick profiles and lower noisy cache evictions.
notes_for_ops: Ops: the new presubmit workflows are behind a temporary feature toggle controlled by org-level repo secret CI_PROFILE_ROLLOUT. Monitor presubmit/cache-hit and runtime dashboards (dashboards/presubmit-runtime). If cache-hit drops by >10% after 24h, revert the rollout toggle. The adapter emits metrics prefixed ci_presubmit_freeze_*.
squash_reason: Multiple iterative commits produced during testing and metric additions; squash for a concise history.
additional_context: This is intentionally conservative: adapters only run in presubmit and produce ephemeral overlays that are ignored by release pipelines. We validated against redwood, redwood-sdk-go and redwood-model-registry to ensure cross-repo cache stability.
